title: Treacle Tart
subtitle: Classic British golden syrup tart with a breadcrumb filling
excerpt: A buttery shortcrust pastry shell filled with a mixture of golden syrup, breadcrumbs, and lemon juice, baked until set with a slight wobble. The quintessentially British tart.

recipe.sourceNotes: Treacle tart is a classic British tart that uses golden syrup (called black treacle in older texts, though the modern dish uses the pale golden syrup) as its primary filling, thickened with fresh or dry breadcrumbs. Despite the name, most modern treacle tarts contain no actual black treacle at all: the term is historical and reflects the fact that golden syrup, introduced commercially in the 1880s, was considered a form of treacle. The tart is one of the most characteristically British of all desserts, with a flavour profile that depends almost entirely on the distinctive taste of Lyle's golden syrup. Lemon juice is added to balance the sweetness. The tart is associated with British school dinners and is notably the favourite dessert of Harry Potter. It is best served warm with clotted cream or custard. The filling should be slightly wobbly when it comes out of the oven: it sets further on cooling.

recipeTools.notes: A 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin, or a regular pie dish.

content.text: Blind-bake the pastry shell before adding the filling: a wet filling in an unbaked pastry shell will produce a soggy base. The breadcrumbs absorb the excess moisture from the syrup and give the filling its characteristic slightly chewy, dense texture. Fresh white breadcrumbs give a lighter result than dried breadcrumbs. The tart is done when the filling is set at the edges and still has a slight tremor in the centre when the tin is gently shaken.

items.preparation: ready-made, or homemade from 200 g plain flour and 100 g cold butter
about 14 tablespoons; weigh the tin before and after
or fresh white breadcrumbs from 3 slices of bread

content.text: Roll the pastry to 3 mm thick and line a 23 cm tart tin. Trim the edges. Chill for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Line the pastry with baking parchment and baking beans and blind-bake for 15 minutes. Remove the paper and beans and bake for a further 5 minutes until pale gold.

Warm the golden syrup very gently in a large saucepan until runny. Remove from the heat. Stir in the breadcrumbs, lemon zest, lemon juice, and cream. Leave to stand for 5 minutes so the breadcrumbs absorb the syrup.

Pour the filling into the pastry case. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the filling is set at the edges and barely trembles in the centre. Rest for 20 minutes. Serve warm with clotted cream or cold with a jug of custard.
